title: Verifier‑Assisted vs. LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Confirmatory Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with up to one automated repair) increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Each pair evaluated a single shared LLM candidate under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); paired contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed=1729, B=10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and model, single‑shot generation was near ceiling, limiting the observable marginal rescue by the guarded pipeline. We archive all execution and analysis artifacts to support replication and follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, or repair budget.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are actively applied to NetOps tasks including intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. Successful operational adoption requires semantic pre‑deployment checks because syntactic validity does not ensure safety properties such as reachability, sequencing constraints, or policy preservation. Prior work reports that generate→validate→repair scaffolds reduce some errors, but reported effect sizes depend on model capability, task hardness, and validator semantics. We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment designed to isolate the marginal effect of a deterministic verifier (plus a bounded repair budget) on an identical LLM candidate per intent. Research question: Does integrating a deterministic verifier into an LLM‑driven change‑generation pipeline increase the probability that an LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation (unflagged) compared with accepting a single‑shot LLM output when both conditions evaluate the same candidate? Our contributions are (1) a preregistered paired evaluation (N=300 pairs) conditioning on a single shared_initial candidate to measure verifier/repair rescue utility; (2) archival of execution and analysis artifacts showing near‑ceiling baseline performance for the chosen synthetic suite, model, and validator; and (3) an evidence‑grounded discussion of estimand interpretation, statistical handling in near‑ceiling regimes, reproducibility mechanics, and operational implications for follow‑up studies.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers demonstrate active interest in LLM applications for network management, intent translation, configuration synthesis, and repair; they also propose planner‑centric and tool‑augmented agentic frameworks that allow invocation of external validators and automated repairs. Representative verified findings used for positioning: (a) LLMs can produce configuration artifacts and intent translations but performance varies by task and dataset; (b) tool‑augmented pipelines (planner‑centric, ReAct variants) enable external validators to check semantics and steer repairs; and (c) generate→validate→repair patterns often improve correctness conditional on validator coverage. Limitations in the prior work include heterogeneity of benchmarks, variable validator expressiveness, and few head‑to‑head controlled comparisons isolating verifier rescue from other scaffold effects. Our study complements these contributions by using a preregistered paired estimand that conditions on a single shared candidate so the measured effect strictly quantifies deterministic verifier/repair rescue of that candidate rather than end‑to‑end pipeline gains that arise from independent alternative model draws.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: We preregistered study cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001 before the confirmatory run. The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) comparing guarded (validator+≤1 repair) and baseline (accept single‑shot) conditions on the same shared_initial candidate. Design and frozen choices: model = gpt-5-mini; validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 executing the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule; task suite = synthetic_topology_suite_v1 produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; per‑pair repair budget ≤1 automated repair attempt; shared_initial generation per pair (one model draw); planned analyzable pairs = 300 (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high). Inclusion/exclusion and missingness rules: pairs were excluded from primary analysis only if both pipeline calls failed due to provider/infrastructure outage; single‑call failures were handled per the executor's complete_pair_primary rule and sensitivity analyses were specified. Analysis plan: confirmatory analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 implementing an exact two‑sided McNemar‑equivalent test and a paired bootstrap percentile CI (B = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729) to produce p‑values and 95% CI for the paired difference. Pilot note (explicit): the preregistration described a pilot (n = 60) for discordance estimation and power calibration; that pilot was not executed and no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed—the pre‑specified main N = 300 was used.

Confirmatory inference (paired_binary_analysis_v1): absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 given m = n10 + n01 = 1 discordant observation; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). The archived validator trace for that episode records that the validator detected a must_be_down_for_fields sequencing violation and that the automated repair inserted the required 'admin down' sequencing step before the VLAN/MTU change; subsequent revalidation reported valid == true. Representative task manifest entries and full validator traces for rescued episodes are archived and summarized in the run bundle.
sections.discussion: Statistical interpretation in near‑ceiling settings: The observed absolute improvement (0.00333) is numerically small because single‑shot LLM generation already satisfied the deterministic validator in 299 of 300 intents. With m = 1 discordant pair, the exact conditional McNemar test yields p = 1.0, which reflects insufficient discordant evidence rather than strong evidence for equality. The paired bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01] bounds the plausible paired improvement under the shared_initial estimand to at most 1 percentage point in this experimental context. Estimand and operational meaning: the shared_initial design intentionally conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate per intent; it therefore isolates the deterministic rescue/repair effect for that candidate and does not measure verifier benefits that could accrue if conditions allowed independent alternative LLM draws per arm (for example, verifier‑guided candidate resampling or model steering). This distinction matters operationally: an organization deciding whether to deploy a validator as an audit+repair layer for a given LLM candidate set (shared_initial) will find our result directly informative, whereas a full pipeline redesign that allows verifier‑guided alternative candidate generation requires a distinct estimand and experiment. Reproducibility and artifact grounding: all raw outputs, provider traces, task manifests, validator traces, analysis CSVs (condition_summary.csv, paired_contingency_table.csv, missingness_summary.csv, contamination_summary.csv), and logs are archived in the run bundle; representative artifact examples (six task artifacts and response traces) are enumerated in the manuscript evidence bundle. Operational implications and follow‑ups: when base models are near‑ceiling relative to a validator suite, bounded verifier+repair (shared_initial) yields limited marginal correctness gain but still provides deterministic audit trails and a targeted repair mechanism for localized sequencing or syntactic omissions. To measure larger pipeline gains, follow‑ups should evaluate (a) independent candidate draws per condition (to capture verifier–model interaction and guided resampling effects), (b) weaker LLMs or intentionally harder/realistic intents to increase discordance, and (c) expanded repair budgets (iterative repairs, ensemble repairs) to quantify repair cost/benefit tradeoffs. Threats to validity (brief): the synthetic benchmark and deterministic task generator may underrepresent real‑world heterogeneity; validator semantics (which constraints are checked) determine observable failure modes; single‑model and single‑validator scope limit external generalizability.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate (shared_initial) on 300 paired synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline single‑shot generation achieved 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding a negligible paired improvement (0.00333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). These results show that measured verifier marginality depends strongly on base model capability, task difficulty, validator semantics, and estimand conditioning. We release the preregistration id, execution and analysis artifacts, representative task manifests, and validator traces in the archived run bundle to support replication and motivate follow‑ups varying estimand choice, model strength, and repair strategies.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/verifier‑diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.

Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot (n = 60) intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration recalculation of required sample size was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition.
Repair budget: guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
